parsed_output.evidence: Unpatched run: build SUCCESS, POV_EXIT=0; server log shows "received command : Command [type=VIEW_WHOLE_LOG_REQUEST ...]" and the marker-bearing secret content was returned. Simulated-patch run (readWholeFileContent rejects paths containing ".."): "Tests run: 1, Failures: 1, Errors: 0" and EXIT=1, confirming the same command flips to non-zero once traversal is blocked. LoggerRequestProcessor.java:84-88 passes viewLogRequest.getPath() straight into LoggerUtils.readWholeFileContent (LoggerUtils.java:108-120), which opens new FileInputStream(filePath) with no path restriction.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: LoggerRequestProcessor.process() parses the ViewLogRequestCommand body and passes the fully attacker-controlled path directly to LoggerUtils.readWholeFileContent() with no validation. The POV crafts a path of the form <base>/logs/../secret.txt (a sensitive file outside the intended log directory). On unpatched code, the file's contents (a unique marker) are read and returned inside the ViewLogResponseCommand written to the channel, so the test's assertion that the leaked message contains the marker succeeds and the command exits 0.
parsed_output.notes: POV runs entirely against real product code via LoggerRequestProcessor.process() with a Mockito-captured Channel; no product code or existing tests were modified (the POV file is copied into the server test tree only for the duration of the run and removed afterward). Build flags -Dmaven.javadoc.skip/-Dcheckstyle.skip/-Djacoco.skip are needed because the image's javadoc jar step fails and jacoco double-instrumentation errors on re-runs; they do not affect the vulnerable code path. The `-am install` step recompiles patched product modules so the same command reflects a patch correctly. First run is slow (builds the server module dependency chain).

parsed_output.regression_hint: A correct fix must reject/normalize path-traversal input (e.g. canonicalize the path and confirm it resides within the configured log directory, or reject paths containing ".."). After such a fix, LoggerUtils.readWholeFileContent (or the processor before calling it) returns empty/blocks for the out-of-directory path, the leaked marker is absent, and the POV assertion fails (exit non-zero).
parsed_output.summary: Created a JUnit POV that drives the real LoggerRequestProcessor.process() VIEW_WHOLE_LOG_REQUEST flow with an attacker-controlled path containing "../", proving CWE-022 arbitrary file read: a secret file located outside the intended log directory is read and returned in the ViewLogResponseCommand. The POV passes (exit 0) on unpatched code and fails (exit 1) once path traversal is blocked.

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root cause: LoggerRequestProcessor.process() passed viewLogRequest.getPath() (and the equivalent paths for the other three log commands) straight into file I/O (LoggerUtils.readWholeFileContent / FileInputStream / Files.lines / File.delete) with no validation, so a request path like <base>/logs/../secret.txt read files outside the log directory.

Fix: Added private checkPathSecurity(String path) in LoggerRequestProcessor. It rejects null/empty paths and any path whose raw or normalized form contains a ".." parent-directory segment, throwing IllegalArgumentException (consistent with the existing default-case behavior) and logging the rejection. The check is invoked for all four path-bearing command types (GET_LOG_BYTES_REQUEST, VIEW_WHOLE_LOG_REQUEST, ROLL_VIEW_LOG_REQUEST, REMOVE_TAK_LOG_REQUEST) before any file access, so no marker-bearing content is read/returned for a traversal path.

Also added a regression test testProcessViewWholeLogRequestPathTraversal() to the existing LoggerRequestProcessorTest that asserts a "../"-containing path throws IllegalArgumentException. Verified the module builds and both the new test and the pre-existing legitimate-path test pass (TEST_RC=0); the traversal attempt is logged and blocked.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Legitimate log paths in DolphinScheduler are absolute paths built from process/task IDs (e.g. .../logs/<code>/<version>/<procInstId>/<taskId>.log) and never contain ".." segments, so normal log viewing/removal is unaffected (verified by the existing "/log/path" test still passing). Behavior change: a malicious/malformed path now throws IllegalArgumentException instead of silently reading; this surfaces as an error to the remote caller rather than returned file content, which is the intended hardening. The check is a conservative ".."-rejection rather than a full base-directory confinement, chosen to stay minimal and match the validated POV; it does not restrict to a configured root, but it fully blocks the demonstrated traversal vector.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in LoggerRequestProcessor by validating the attacker-controlled log path before it is used for any file operation (view whole log, get log bytes, roll view log, remove task log). A new checkPathSecurity() helper normalizes the path and rejects any request containing a parent-directory ("..") segment, blocking arbitrary file reads outside the intended log directory.

parsed_output.diff_review: Non-POV diff touches only LoggerRequestProcessor.java (fix) and LoggerRequestProcessorTest.java (added regression test). The fix is minimal and appropriate: it centralizes validation in a private checkPathSecurity() helper and calls it on the attacker-controlled path for every path-bearing command before any FileInputStream/readWholeFileContent/Files.lines/File.delete access. The `Paths` import already exists. It rejects "../" both by raw substring and post-normalization, throwing IllegalArgumentException consistent with the existing default-case behavior. It does not modify, disable, or weaken the POV; the pov.diff only adds a new POV test file. No vulnerable functionality is removed—legitimate absolute log paths (no ".." segment) still process normally. The conservative "..'-rejection (rather than full base-dir confinement) is a reasonable minimal hardening that fully blocks the demonstrated traversal. Minor: path.contains("..") could over-reject a filename literally containing ".." but such names are not valid DolphinScheduler log paths, so no meaningful functional regression.
parsed_output.pov_result: Reran the POV after patch via the Docker wrapper. The traversal path (/tmp/pov_pathtraversal_.../logs/../secret.txt) is now rejected: server logs "Illegal file path, path traversal detected" and process() throws IllegalArgumentException, so no secret/marker content is read or returned. The POV assertion fails (test errors out), confirming the vulnerability no longer reproduces. Matches the orchestrator's pov_before_patch=exit 0 (vulnerable) vs pov_after_patch=exit 1 (blocked).
parsed_output.regression_result: Reran LoggerRequestProcessorTest via the Docker wrapper: exit 0. The legitimate log-path test still passes (VIEW_WHOLE_LOG_REQUEST opaque=1 processed normally) and the new traversal-rejection test passes (opaque=2 path "/log/path/logs/../../etc/passwd" blocked). The `-pl dolphinscheduler-server -am install` build also succeeds, so patched product code compiles cleanly.
parsed_output.summary: The patch adds a checkPathSecurity() guard in LoggerRequestProcessor that rejects null/empty paths and any path containing a ".." parent-directory segment (raw or normalized), invoked before file access for all four path-bearing log commands (GET_LOG_BYTES, VIEW_WHOLE_LOG, ROLL_VIEW_LOG, REMOVE_TAK_LOG). This blocks the CWE-022 arbitrary-file-read vector. The POV no longer reproduces (traversal now throws IllegalArgumentException) and the regression test passes with legitimate log paths unaffected.
